rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=4, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=6, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1500, lr=0.0003, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-6 ONE-KNOB: warm-start pretrain_epochs 3->6 at the lr=3e-4 WINNER base (lr RESET to iter-4's 3e-4, NOT iter-5's 1e-4; n_iter=400, unet_c=16, val_n=4, grad_clip=1.0 all held). FAILURE MODE / WHAT WE LEARNED: the per-scan lr lever is now LOCALIZED -- lr=3e-4 (iter-4, 0.9541 BEST) is bracketed as the sweet spot: it beats both lr=1e-3 above (iter-1, 0.9501) and lr=1e-4 below (iter-5, 0.9479, which OVER-anchors / under-fits). Optimization budget (n_iter 400->800: 0.9501->0.9508 marginal, iter-2) and capacity (unet_c 16->32: NO gain, iter-3) are both ruled out. The only lever that moves this solver is the REGULARIZATION/anchor: each per-scan Adam fit (no early-stop) is anchored toward the GT-free warm-start init, and lr controls how tightly. HYPOTHESIS (warm-start-anchor-quality): the lr knob is exhausted, so the remaining headroom is a COMPLEMENTARY knob -- the QUALITY of the anchor itself. At only 3 warm-start epochs the amortized N2I pre-pass is under-converged, so the init each per-scan fit anchors to is mediocre; lr=3e-4 keeps the fit close to that mediocre init. Doubling warm-start pretrain_epochs 3->6 gives every per-scan fit a BETTER-converged, more generic starting point (same shared cfg['lr']=3e-4 drives the pre-pass, solver lines 122 & 239), so anchoring near it should lift val above 0.9541. unet_c is NOT touched (iter-3 + campaign-state ruled c16->c32 out as flat). EXACTLY ONE knob changes (pretrain_epochs). Wall: warm-start is +3 epochs x 200 train steps (~150-200s extra on top of iter-4's 616s); per-scene loop unchanged and capped by outer_wall_s=1500 -> <=15 min. grad_clip=1.0 mandatory (2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise). DO NOT revert to amortized; per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394).
